en.title: Arrange Coins
en.description:
Given several non-negative integers coins. For each n, place coins row by row starting from the first row: row 1 needs 1 coin, row 2 needs 2 coins, and so on. Only completely filled rows count; find the maximum number of rows each n can fill.

The explicit standard input/output format and supplementary constraints on this site belong to the online version and are not presented as the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line is the array length N, and the second line contains N integers. Site constraints: 1≤N≤100000, 0≤coins[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output N integers, the number of rows each coins[i] can fill, in order.
en.explanation: For each n, find the largest k such that 1+2+…+k = k(k+1)/2 ≤ n. You can binary search on k, using integer multiplication in the check to avoid floating-point rounding.
hints: For each n, find the largest k such that 1+2+…+k = k(k+1)/2 ≤ n. You can binary search on k, using integer multiplication in the check to avoid floating-point rounding.
